These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize() for money; always round with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), as line_total and invoice_total do.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize money via to_money and round_money: In ledgerly/invoice.py, convert any monetary input with to_money() and store it rounded with round_money(); compare against ZERO from ledgerly.money rather than raw numbers.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors with codes like "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount", matching the pattern used in issue_invoice.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

item.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc before comparing
item.content: In ledgerly, always pass datetimes through `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` before arithmetic or comparison (as `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py` does); never compare raw `sub.started_at` or caller-supplied datetimes directly.

candidate.content: Signal invalid billing inputs by raising `ledgerly.errors.BillingError` with a short snake_case code string (e.g. "invalid_period", "before_start") plus a repr of the offending value, rather than ValueError or bare exceptions.

candidate.title: Compute period index via floor division on timedelta
candidate.content: To locate a billing period, compute `n = (at - start) // length` with `length = timedelta(days=sub.period_days)` and offset from `start`, mirroring `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`; do not use day counts or modulo arithmetic.
